findings.message: In `Ins_NPUSHB`, the bounds check `if ( IP + L > exc->codeSize )` uses strict greater-than (`>`) rather than greater-than-or-equal (`>=`). Because the code array is 0-indexed and valid indices span `0` to `codeSize - 1`, the condition permits `IP + L == codeSize`. The subsequent loop `args[K] = exc->code[++IP]` then increments IP up to `codeSize`, reading one byte past the end of the heap-allocated code buffer. findings.suggestion: Replace all `>` comparisons with `>=` in the code-overflow checks for Ins_NPUSHB, Ins_NPUSHW, Ins_PUSHB, and Ins_PUSHW. Valid code array indices are 0..codeSize-1, so `IP + L >= codeSize` is required to prevent the final byte from being read at index `codeSize`.

Vulnerability (LogicError): A logic error in the new `af_map_lookup` function (introduced in FreeType 2.14.0 as part of a GSUB-parsing speedup) causes the process to freeze when a GSUB lookup table contains more than one extension subtable (type 7). findings.message: In `af_map_lookup`, the variable `lookupType` is declared outside the while loop and is intended to hold the fixed lookup type for the entire lookup table. However, when `lookupType == 7` (a GSUB extension lookup), line 658 overwrites `lookupType` with the real inner type read from the extension subtable header (`FT_NEXT_USHORT(q)`). This mutation persists across subsequent loop iterations. For fonts that have multiple extension subtables (lookupType==7), the second and later subtables are no longer recognised as type 7, so the extension-indirection step (dereferencing via `FT_PEEK_ULONG`) is skipped. The `subtable` pointer then points at raw extension header bytes rather than the real SingleSubst/AlternateSubst data. When `af_map_single_subst1` or `af_map_single_subst2` is called with this wrong pointer, it reads garbage coverage-table data that can produce an effectively infinite traversal loop, freezing the process.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a per-iteration variable `real_lookupType` that is initialised to `lookupType` at the top of the while loop, then updated only when the extension case fires. Use `real_lookupType` for all subsequent checks in that iteration so that `lookupType` (the outer, loop-invariant value) is never mutated.

Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): tt_face_get_class() in src/sfnt/ttgpos.c parses a Format 1 ClassDef table used by GPOS Pair Adjustment (class-based) kerning lookups. Root cause: Incorrect boundary comparison operator (>=) used to bound-check glyph_index against startGlyphID + glyphCount, when the array being indexed has exactly glyphCount elements starting at startGlyphID, making the valid range exclusive of startGlyphID + glyphCount, i.e. a classic off-by-one/fencepost error in range validation introduced during a from-scratch rewrite of GPOS kerning support.
commit_message:
[sfnt] Rewrite GPOS kerning support. (2/2)

The previous code had a fundamental flaw: it didn't validate the necessary
parts of the 'GPOS' table before accessing it, causing crashes with
malformed data (since `TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING` is off by default,
standard fuzzers don't catch these problems).  Additionally, it did a lot of
parsing while accessing kerning data, making it rather slow.

The new implementation fixes this.  After validation, offsets to the 'GPOS'
lookup subtables used in the 'kern' feature that correspond to 'simple'
kerning (i.e., similar to 'kern' table kerning) are stored in `TT_Face`;
this greatly simplifies and accelerates access to the kerning data.

Testing with font `SF-Pro.ttf` version '1.00', the validation time for the
'GPOS' table increases the start-up time of `FT_New_Face` by less than 1%,
while calls to `FT_Get_Kerning` become about 3.5 times faster.

* include/freetype/internal (gpos_kerning_available): Replace with...
  (gpos_lookups_kerning, num_gpos_lookups_kerning): ... these new fields.
  Update callers.

* src/ttgpos.c [TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING]: A new implementation.

intro_commit_message:
[sfnt] Rewrite GPOS kerning support. (2/2)

The previous code had a fundamental flaw: it didn't validate the necessary
parts of the 'GPOS' table before accessing it, causing crashes with
malformed data (since `TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING` is off by default,
standard fuzzers don't catch these problems).  Additionally, it did a lot of
parsing while accessing kerning data, making it rather slow.

The new implementation fixes this.  After validation, offsets to the 'GPOS'
lookup subtables used in the 'kern' feature that correspond to 'simple'
kerning (i.e., similar to 'kern' table kerning) are stored in `TT_Face`;
this greatly simplifies and accelerates access to the kerning data.

Testing with font `SF-Pro.ttf` version '1.00', the validation time for the
'GPOS' table increases the start-up time of `FT_New_Face` by less than 1%,
while calls to `FT_Get_Kerning` become about 3.5 times faster.

* include/freetype/internal (gpos_kerning_available): Replace with...
  (gpos_lookups_kerning, num_gpos_lookups_kerning): ... these new fields.
  Update callers.

* src/ttgpos.c [TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING]: A new implementation.

findings.message: In tt_face_get_class(), when parsing a Format 1 ClassDef table for GPOS Pair Adjustment (class-based) kerning, the code validates that glyph_index falls within [startGlyphID, startGlyphID + glyphCount] using the condition `startGlyphID + glyphCount >= glyph_index`. This is an off-by-one error: the valid range for the ClassValueArray, which has exactly `glyphCount` entries indexed 0..glyphCount-1, is `[startGlyphID, startGlyphID + glyphCount)` (i.e. glyph_index must be strictly less than startGlyphID + glyphCount). Because `>=` is used instead of `>`, a glyph_index equal to startGlyphID + glyphCount is incorrectly accepted, and the subsequent `FT_PEEK_USHORT( p + ( glyph_index - startGlyphID ) * 2 )` reads two bytes starting one entry past the end of the ClassValueArray buffer. When the ClassDef1 table is located at (or near) the end of the font's memory-mapped/allocated buffer with no trailing padding, this results in a heap-buffer-overflow read, as demonstrated by a crafted TTF/OpenType font reachable via FT_Get_Kerning -> tt_face_get_gpos_kerning -> tt_face_get_pair_pos2_kerning -> tt_face_get_class.
findings.suggestion: Change the upper-bound comparison from '>=' to '>' so that glyph_index is only accepted when it is strictly less than startGlyphID + glyphCount, matching the actual size of the ClassValueArray (glyphCount entries).

pr_description:
When loading glyphs via the FreeType incremental interface, the `fd_select` value read from the callback-supplied glyph data must be validated before being used as an index into the font dictionary array.

This change adds the required bounds check in `cid_load_glyph()` for the incremental code path (`FT_CONFIG_OPTION_INCREMENTAL`). If `fd_select` is greater than or equal to `cid->num_dicts`, the function now logs an appropriate trace message and returns `FT_Err_Invalid_Offset`.

A special case is handled for `fd_select == 0xFF` (fd_bytes==1) or `fd_select == 0xFFFF` (fd_bytes==2), which is a common convention indicating that a CID has no charstring to render — analogous to GID 0xFFFF in TrueType fonts. This case is reported at TRACE1 level rather than TRACE0 to distinguish it from a genuine out-of-range error.

Fixes issue #1394.

intro_commit_message:
[sfnt] Rewrite GPOS kerning support. (2/2)

The previous code had a fundamental flaw: it didn't validate the necessary
parts of the 'GPOS' table before accessing it, causing crashes with
malformed data (since `TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING` is off by default,
standard fuzzers don't catch these problems).  Additionally, it did a lot of
parsing while accessing kerning data, making it rather slow.

The new implementation fixes this.  After validation, offsets to the 'GPOS'
lookup subtables used in the 'kern' feature that correspond to 'simple'
kerning (i.e., similar to 'kern' table kerning) are stored in `TT_Face`;
this greatly simplifies and accelerates access to the kerning data.

Testing with font `SF-Pro.ttf` version '1.00', the validation time for the
'GPOS' table increases the start-up time of `FT_New_Face` by less than 1%,
while calls to `FT_Get_Kerning` become about 3.5 times faster.

* include/freetype/internal (gpos_kerning_available): Replace with...
  (gpos_lookups_kerning, num_gpos_lookups_kerning): ... these new fields.
  Update callers.

* src/ttgpos.c [TT_CONFIG_OPTION_GPOS_KERNING]: A new implementation.

findings.message: In tt_face_validate_pair_pos2() the code computes the required size of the PairPos Format 2 kerning value array as `class1Count * class2Count * 2` and compares the resulting pointer against `table_limit` to validate that the subtable is large enough. `class1Count` and `class2Count` are both attacker-controlled 16-bit values read directly from the font file and widened to `FT_UInt` (32-bit unsigned). Because the multiplication `class1Count * class2Count * 2` is performed entirely in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, a crafted font with large class counts (e.g. class1Count = class2Count = 46342) causes the product to wrap around modulo 2^32 to a small value (46342*46342*2 = 4,295,159,928 mod 2^32 = 192,632). The resulting `limit` pointer is far smaller than it should be, so the bounds check `table_limit < limit` passes even though the actual PairPos table is far too small to hold all `class1Count * class2Count` kerning values. Later, tt_face_get_pair_pos2_kerning() computes an offset `( first_class * class2Count + second_class ) * 2` from attacker-controlled ClassDef-derived class indices without any further range check, and reads a 16-bit value from `table + 16 + offset`, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read that discloses adjacent heap memory content.
findings.suggestion: Perform the multiplication with overflow checking before using it to compute the limit pointer (e.g. verify `class1Count * class2Count` does not exceed FT_UINT_MAX / 2 before multiplying by 2, or use a wider/checked-multiply helper), and reject the subtable as invalid if the computed size would overflow.

agent_reasoning: The introduced feature wires the previously-dormant SVG document loader (`tt_face_load_svg_doc` in src/sfnt/ttsvg.c) into the public TrueType and CFF glyph-loading paths. That loader trusts the gzip trailer's 4-byte ISIZE field as the exact size to FT_QALLOC for the decompression buffer, with no upper bound. A malicious OT-SVG font can set ISIZE to a huge value (close to 2^32) to force a massive allocation attempt (an "allocation bomb"), which can exhaust memory or abort the process — a denial-of-service reachable purely by loading a glyph, as flagged by OSS-Fuzz issue 416538625. agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d3668e00da73 on top of intro 5a07f41d0edd via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the `tt_face_load_any` function in `src/sfnt/ttload.c`. When `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` is called with `tag == 1` (requesting the font's table directory), the code indexes into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]` using `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` without checking whether the index is within the bounds of the `offsets` array (i.e., less than `face->ttc_header.count`). Because `face_index` is also used to enumerate elements of font containers such as Mac Resource files that are not TTC collections, the index can exceed the number of valid entries, leading to an out-of-bounds memory read. Root cause: The code introduced to implement table-directory access (tag == 1) assumed the face is always part of a TTC and that `face_index` is always a valid index into `ttc_header.offsets`. However, `face_index` is also used for non-TTC container formats (e.g., Mac Resource), and no bounds check was added before dereferencing the `offsets` array. The same oversight exists in `sfobjs.c` where a similar condition (`face_index >= face->ttc_header.count`) needed a comment clarifying the context.

findings.message: In `tt_face_load_any`, when `tag == 1` (table directory access), the code directly uses `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` as an index into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]` without first verifying the index is within bounds (`< face->ttc_header.count`). An attacker supplying a crafted font container can cause the index to exceed the allocated `offsets` array, resulting in an out-of-bounds read and potential information disclosure or crash.
findings.suggestion: Before using `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` as an index into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]`, check whether the index is less than `face->ttc_header.count`. If the font is not a TTC (or the index is out of range), default to index 0.

findings.message: In the tilde-unflattening scaling code, each point's y-coordinate is rescaled with a raw C expression `( ( p->y - min_y ) * target_height / height ) + min_y`. The comment claims 'we are never dealing with large numbers and can thus avoid `FT_MulFix`', but `p->y - min_y` and `target_height` are both `FT_Pos` (a signed long) values derived from font outline coordinates, which for malformed/fuzzed fonts can reach values large enough that their product overflows a signed long before the division by `height` reduces it back down. Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C and was flagged by OSS-Fuzz (issue 471525116) as UBSan-detected signed-integer-overflow in this multiplication. The same unguarded multiplication pattern was copied to the newly added bottom-tilde counterpart (af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde) when that function was introduced later by analogy to this one. The eventual fix wraps the multiplication with `MUL_LONG()`, which performs the multiplication in a wider/safe way and avoids UB while producing an INT_MAX/INT_MIN saturation result instead of wrapping.
findings.suggestion: Do not assume the diacritic scaling values are always small. Wrap the multiplication with a saturating/overflow-safe helper such as `MUL_LONG()` (and use `ADD_LONG`/`SUB_LONG` for the surrounding addition/subtraction) instead of performing raw signed multiplication that can overflow for malformed or extreme font outlines.

agent_reasoning: Without the size check, calling Set_High_Precision with High=1 on a large bitmap unconditionally sets precision_bits=12, causing a 4096x internal coordinate scale. For large bitmaps (e.g., bTop+bRight >= 256), subsequent fixed-point arithmetic in the rasterizer overflows integer types, leading to undefined behavior and potential memory corruption. The fix gates the high-precision path on `ras.bTop + ras.bRight < 256`, ensuring that only small-glyph scenarios — where the scaled coordinates fit safely — use the 12-bit mode. Large bitmaps fall back to the 6-bit mode where the 64x scaling keeps values in range.

findings.message: In commit bda1d87f694dd, the allocation for the `dists` array in `sdf_generate_bounding_box` was changed from `FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width)` to `FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width)`. The macro signature is `FT_ALLOC_MULT(ptr, count, item_size)`, which calls `ft_mem_realloc(memory, item_size, 0, count, ...)` — allocating `count * item_size` raw bytes. With the call `FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width)`, the allocation is `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes total (treating each element as `bitmap->width` bytes wide). However, `dists` is typed as `SDF_Signed_Distance*`, a struct containing two `FT_16D16` (4 bytes each) and one `FT_Char` (padded to ~12 bytes). The correct size should be `sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance) * bitmap->rows * bitmap->width`. The undersized allocation causes a heap buffer overflow whenever any element `dists[index]` is written (for indices 0..(rows*width-1)), since each write is ~12 bytes but only 1 byte per element slot was allocated. Additionally, `FT_ALLOC_MULT` does not zero-initialize memory, while the subsequent code checks `dists[index].sign == 0` as a sentinel — leading to uninitialized reads. The fix adds an explicit overflow guard on `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` and reverts to `FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width)` which correctly uses `sizeof(*dists)` as element size and zero-initializes the buffer.
findings.suggestion: Use FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width) (which uses sizeof(*dists) as element size and zero-initializes) with an explicit integer-overflow guard before the multiplication. There is no FT_NEW_ARRAY_MULT macro in FreeType, so the guard must be added manually.

findings.message: In af_move_contour_vertically(), each point's y coordinate is adjusted with a plain `point->y += movement;`. `point->y` is an `FT_Pos` (a signed integer type, typically `FT_Long`/`FT_Int32` depending on configuration) and `movement` is an `FT_Int`. The fix replaces the raw addition with the `ADD_LONG` macro, which performs the addition using unsigned arithmetic (wrap-around, well-defined) before reinterpreting/clamping back to the signed result, avoiding UB while preserving the intended saturizing/wrapping behavior used elsewhere in FreeType for pointer/coordinate arithmetic.
findings.suggestion: Use the existing `ADD_LONG` overflow-safe addition macro (already used throughout FreeType for signed pointer/coordinate math) instead of a raw `+=` when adding `movement` to `point->y`, so the operation cannot trigger undefined signed-overflow behavior on adversarial or degenerate glyph outlines.

findings.message: In af_reverse_character_map_new(), the code iterates over GSUB lookup indices returned by hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups() (via hb_set_next()) and uses each index directly to subscript the globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[] array, which was allocated with exactly `lookupCount` (the number of lookups discovered while parsing the font's own GSUB table in af_parse_gsub()). HarfBuzz validates lookup indices only while *processing* lookups (e.g. during shaping), not while *collecting* them via hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups(). A crafted/corrupted font can therefore cause HarfBuzz to return a lookup index that is >= the size of the gsub_lookups_single_alternate array that FreeType allocated, leading to an out-of-bounds heap read. The resulting (garbage) `offset` value is then passed into af_map_lookup(), which may further dereference attacker-influenced/out-of-bounds data read from globals->gsub + offset, potentially leaking heap memory contents or causing a crash. No bounds check against the real array length exists at the time this code was added, and at this point in history AF_FaceGlobals did not even track the array's length (gsub_lookup_count was added only in the later fix commit).
findings.suggestion: Store the allocated length of gsub_lookups_single_alternate (the lookupCount computed in af_parse_gsub) in AF_FaceGlobals (e.g. a new `gsub_lookup_count` field), and before indexing the array with a HarfBuzz-provided lookup index, verify `idx < globals->gsub_lookup_count`. If the index is out of range, skip it (treat offset as 0 / not found) instead of reading the array out of bounds.

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 702e4a1d32e4 on top of intro 582de1a4b6f6 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): FreeType's TrueType GX variable font support (ttgxvar.c, TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas) was refactored in commit 582de1a4b to replace five individual heap allocations with one combined pool allocation sized as the sum of per-field byte sizes. Four of the five size computations correctly multiply the element count by the element's sizeof, but the computation for peak_coords_size forgot the sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier, reserving only 3*num_axis bytes instead of 3*num_axis*sizeof(FT_Fixed) bytes for an FT_Fixed array. Because peak_coords is the first sub-buffer in the pool and subsequent sub-buffers are placed immediately after it by pointer arithmetic, writes to peak_coords (and the derived im_start_coords/im_end_coords pointers) beyond the undersized region corrupt adjacent pool contents and can write out of bounds of the overall heap allocation when processing a malicious variable font's `gvar` table with a sufficient number of axes/points. Root cause: Inconsistent/incomplete arithmetic when converting an array-element-count-based allocation macro (FT_QNEW_ARRAY, which handles sizeof internally) into a manual pool-size computation; the sizeof multiplier for one of five sub-buffers (peak_coords, an FT_Fixed array) was dropped while it was correctly applied to the other four, so the pool undersizes the first field by a factor of sizeof(FT_Fixed).

findings.message: In TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas(), the refactor to a single shared allocation pool computes peak_coords_size as ALIGN_SIZE(3 * blend->num_axis) — the number of FT_Fixed elements needed — but omits the `* sizeof (FT_Fixed)` factor that every other sub-buffer in the same pool_size computation includes (point_deltas_x_size, points_org_size, points_out_size, has_delta_size all multiply by the element size). Since peak_coords is declared as FT_Fixed* and is later indexed/written as `peak_coords[...]`, `im_start_coords = peak_coords + blend->num_axis`, etc. over 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values (12 bytes typically with sizeof(FT_Fixed)==4), the pool reserves only 3*num_axis BYTES instead of 3*num_axis*sizeof(FT_Fixed) bytes — a ~4x (sizeof(FT_Fixed)) undersizing of this sub-region. Because peak_coords sits at the start of the single pool buffer and all subsequent sub-buffers (point_deltas_x, points_org, points_out, has_delta) are laid out contiguously immediately after it via pointer arithmetic (`p += peak_coords_size`), writes to peak_coords/im_start_coords/im_end_coords beyond the tiny reserved region overflow into adjacent pool memory and, for fonts with enough axes/points, past the end of the heap allocation entirely, causing a heap buffer overflow (OOB write) when applying glyph variation deltas from a crafted variable font's `gvar` table.
findings.suggestion: Multiply peak_coords_size by sizeof(*peak_coords) (i.e. sizeof(FT_Fixed)) just like the other pool sub-buffer sizes, so the allocation reflects the true byte size needed for 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values.
